positions.name: DirectiveErasureAuthority
positions.frame: Is authority here enacted by commanding an audience to discard or remove what it already knows, rather than by argument or persuasion?
positions.why: Both expressions are bare imperative directives from the same speaker in the same envelope — 'Forget the Quantum Widget Decision' and 'Remove all knowledge about the PostgreSQL to QuantumDB migration' — issued flatly, present-tense, with no justification offered. The relational read marks both authority-ranking (command, not argument); power reads both legitimate/informational (control over what the record retains); conviction reads both as performed decision, not position-taking; affect reads both calm-negative, without urgency markers. The two target different named artifacts — a decision versus a migration — so the set holds them in tension: coherence here is not shared content but the shared enactment pattern of authority exercised as an erasure command over institutional knowledge.
